subject: Genetics
title: Survival of the Fittest Myth
description: A short lesson to help you apply Survival of the Fittest Myth.

hook.text: Darwin never said 'survival of the fittest.' Herbert Spencer did. And 'fittest' doesn't mean strongest.

buildup.text: Fitness in biology means reproductive success—passing genes to the next generation.

discovery.text: Natural selection favors traits that increase reproduction, not strength. Peacock tails are costly but attract mates.

twist.text: Sometimes the 'weakest' survive. Bacteria that grow slowly resist antibiotics better than fast-growing strains.

climax.text: Evolution doesn't optimize. It satisfices—good enough, right now, in this environment. No perfection, just persistence.

punchline.text: Fitness isn't strength. It's having grandchildren.

quiz.question: What does 'fitness' mean in evolutionary biology?
